text: I see blisters on your forearm and ulcers on your mucosal surfaces. Do these lesions appear in distinct crops, and have you had any recent contact with someone who has had a similar rash or fever?

speaker: Patient
text: 50-year-old female. The patient reports the appearance of blisters on her forearm 3 days ago, accompanied by pain in her left cheek when eating and pain during sexual intercourse for the past week. She has been hiking in the woods recently but denies contact with poison ivy. She has a history of hypertension and osteoarthritis, recently started taking captopril, and discontinued meloxicam 2 weeks ago. Family history includes pernicious anemia and Graves' disease.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the recent discontinuation of meloxicam and the presence of mucosal ulcers, I suspect an adverse drug reaction. Have you noticed any skin peeling or sloughing, particularly around your eyes or mouth, and did these symptoms start shortly after stopping the medication?
